summary:
Neither store will accept a public, real-money Vaultwise from a student team. Apple 5.1.1(ix) and 3.2.1(viii) say banking, investing and money-management apps should be submitted by the legal entity or financial institution that provides the service, not by an individual. Apple 2.2 says demos and betas belong on TestFlight, not the App Store. Google Play says providers of financial products should use an organization account, which needs a D-U-N-S number. Play also requires an accurate Financial features declaration and compliance with local law in every targeted country. A university organization account fixes the account type but not the licensing.

The compliant fallback is a no-real-money "Practice" build: no bank link, simulated balances, a sandbox merchant checkout and practice-only Satellite. Distribute it through TestFlight (100 internal / 10,000 external testers), Play internal testing (100) or closed testing (12 testers for 14 days on new personal accounts), and Android limited distribution (20 devices).

Required in any build: an 18+ rating (Apple override; Play 18+ audience plus Restrict Minor Access), disclosure and explicit consent before data goes to Groq, an in-app AI report button, account deletion both in-app and on the web, privacy labels and Data safety, privacy manifests, and the system photo picker. Pay with Vaultwise for physical goods is outside IAP and Play Billing. iOS NFC is out of reach, so use QR codes.

findings.claim: Apple expects apps in banking and financial services to be submitted by the legal entity that provides the service, not by an individual developer. As of the 13 Nov 2025 update, crypto exchanges are also on this list.
findings.evidence: 5.1.1(ix): 'Apps that provide services in highly regulated fields (such as banking and financial services, healthcare, gambling, legal cannabis use, air travel and crypto exchanges) or that require sensitive user information should be submitted by a legal entity that provides the services, and not by an individual developer.' The guidelines page says it was last updated 8 June 2026.

findings.claim: Apple expects investing and money-management apps to be submitted by the financial institution performing the service, with licences in every storefront where the app is offered.
findings.evidence: 3.2.1(viii): 'Apps used for financial trading, investing, or money management should be submitted by the financial institution performing such services and must have necessary licensing and permissions in the locations where you make them available.'

findings.claim: Under Apple 2.2, demo, beta and trial builds do not belong on the App Store. TestFlight builds should still be intended for public distribution and comply with the Guidelines.
findings.evidence: 2.2: 'Demos, betas, and trial versions of your app don't belong on the App Store – use TestFlight instead. Any app submitted for beta distribution via TestFlight should be intended for public distribution and should comply with the App Review Guidelines.'

findings.claim: TestFlight allows 100 internal testers, who must be App Store Connect users, and 10,000 external testers. The first build sent to external testers goes through App Review, and builds expire after 90 days.
findings.evidence: From the Apple pages: 'up to 100 App Store Connect users'; 'up to 10,000 people'; 'When you add the first build of your app to a group, the build gets sent to App Review'; 'If you invite external testers, your beta build may require review'; 'You can test a build for up to 90 days.'

findings.claim: Apple organization enrollment needs a legal entity, a D-U-N-S number, a public website and someone with authority to bind the organization. An individual account shows the developer's legal name as the seller. Accredited educational institutions can request a fee waiver if they sell no paid apps or IAP.
findings.evidence: The enroll page states: 'must be a legal entity'; 'must have a D-U-N-S Number'; for individuals, 'Your name will be displayed as the seller name.' The fee-waiver page lists 'accredited educational institution', 'Not be an individual, sole proprietor', and the condition that the Paid Applications Agreement is not signed.

findings.claim: Google Play says developers who provide financial products and services, including banking, loans, stock trading and investment funds, should choose an organization account. Organization accounts need a D-U-N-S number, which can take up to 30 days.
findings.evidence: From the account-type page: 'You should choose an organization account if you provide any of the following services: Financial products and services, including but not limited to banking, loans, stock trading, investment funds, cryptocurrency software wallets, and cryptocurrency exchanges.' From the account-information page: 'You will not be able to create a developer account for an organization without one' (D-U-N-S), with processing of up to 30 days.

findings.claim: Every app on Play must complete the Financial features declaration, including apps on closed and open testing tracks. Vaultwise's features fall into the declaration's categories such as Banking, Mobile payments and digital wallets, Money transfer, Stock trading and portfolio management, and Financial advice.
findings.evidence: 'All developers that have an app published on Google Play must complete the Financial features declaration', which covers closed testing, open testing and production. The category list includes 'Mobile payments and digital wallets', 'Stock trading and portfolio management', 'Financial advice' and 'Banking'.

findings.claim: Play's Financial Services policy requires compliance with local regulations in every targeted country. Its scope includes personalized financial advice. Its only country-specific sections cover personal loans in the US, India, Indonesia, Philippines, Nigeria, Kenya, Pakistan and Thailand. Nothing specific to the UK, Singapore, Australia, UAE, Canada or the euro area appears on that page.
findings.evidence: The policy says 'you must comply with state and local regulations for any region or country that your app targets.' It defines scope as products 'related to the management or investment of money and cryptocurrencies, including personalized advice.' The country-specific list is limited to the loan markets above.

findings.claim: In India, any Play app that offers or facilitates personal loans must appear on the RBI list 'DLAs deployed by Regulated Entities'. New apps have needed this since 30 Oct 2025 and existing apps since 28 Jan 2026.
findings.evidence: The Play Help article sets out the RBI Digital Lending Directions 2025 timeline. It says new personal loan apps must be on the list before publishing, and existing apps must be listed 'before January 28, 2026'. Facilitators of NBFC or bank lending are covered as well.

findings.claim: Personal Play accounts created after 13 Nov 2023 must run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in continuously for 14 days before they can apply for production. Internal testing allows 100 testers and may not go through standard policy review.
findings.evidence: From the testing-requirements page: 'a minimum of 12 testers who have been opted in continuously for at least 14 days'. From the testing-tracks page: 'An internal test can have up to 100 testers per app' and internal tests 'might not be subject to standard Play policy or security reviews'. Apps active only on internal tracks are exempt from Data safety.

findings.claim: Android developer verification protections start on 30 Sep 2026 in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand, with global rollout in 2027. Free limited-distribution accounts let students share apps with up to 20 devices without a government ID.
findings.evidence: The limited-distribution guide says: 'Share apps with up to 20 devices'; 'This account is free'; 'you don't need to provide a government ID'; and 'Any package names not registered by this date will no longer be installable on certified Android devices in those regions.'

findings.claim: Apple's current age-rating tiers are 4+, 9+, 13+, 16+ and 18+. An app whose EULA sets a higher minimum age than Apple's calculated rating must use the override, so an 18+ fintech has to override to 18+.
findings.evidence: From the set-a-rating page: 'If your app has a EULA with minimum age requirements that exceed the rating that Apple calculated, you must override to a rating that adheres to the requirements.' Questionnaire answers have been required since 31 Jan 2026, and the new social-media questions become required from Sept 2026.

findings.claim: Since 24 Feb 2026 the App Store blocks downloads of 18+ apps in Australia, Brazil and Singapore unless the user is confirmed as an adult. Texas (from 4 Jun 2026), Utah (6 May 2026) and Louisiana (1 Jul 2026) impose age-assurance duties for new accounts, and Apple provides the Declared Age Range API for them.
findings.evidence: Apple's news says: 'Apple will block users in Australia, Brazil, and Singapore from downloading apps rated 18+ unless they have been confirmed to be adults'. It adds that developers 'may have separate obligations'. The Texas SB 2420 notice covers new Apple Accounts from June 4, 2026.

findings.claim: In Play Console, a developer can target only 'Ages 18 and over' and turn on Restrict Minor Access for adult-only apps. The Play Age Signals API returns signals for Texas accounts created after 28 May 2026 and for Brazil.
findings.evidence: From the target-audience page: 'If your app is only suitable or designed for an adult audience, you can enable the Restrict Minor Access feature to restrict minors from your app.' The Age Signals overview names Texas SB2420 and Brazil's Digital ECA.

findings.claim: Apple requires apps to disclose clearly when personal data is shared with third-party AI and to get explicit permission first. This was added on 13 Nov 2025. Google Play requires in-app reporting or flagging for generative-AI apps where chatting is a central feature.
findings.evidence: Apple 5.1.2(i): 'You must clearly disclose where personal data will be shared with third parties, including with third-party AI, and obtain explicit permission before doing so.' Play's AI-Generated Content policy says apps 'must contain in-app user reporting or flagging features' so users can report 'without needing to exit the app'.

findings.claim: On Apple, paying for physical goods or services must use a method other than IAP. On Play, Google Play Billing must not be used for physical goods, physical services or peer-to-peer payments.
findings.evidence: Apple 3.1.3(e): '...you must use purchase methods other than in-app purchase to collect those payments, such as Apple Pay or traditional credit card entry.' Play Payments Section 3: 'Google Play's billing system must not be used in cases where:' the purchase is of physical goods or physical services, and the excluded payments 'include peer-to-peer payments'.

findings.claim: In-store NFC payments on iPhone are only open to licensed organizations. HCE is EEA-only and requires an EEA-established organization with regulatory permission. The NFC & SE Platform (US, UK, Canada and Australia from iOS 18.1; Singapore and UAE from 18.4; India from 26.0) requires a financial institution or a binding agreement with a licensed payment service provider, plus a commercial agreement with Apple.
findings.evidence: The HCE page says the developer must be 'enrolled as an organization' and hold 'the legal right and the necessary regulatory permissions to provide mobile payment solutions in the EEA'. The NFC & SE page lists the territories and states the licence or PSP-agreement requirement and 'any applicable fees'.

findings.claim: Account deletion is required on both stores. Apple wants full deletion in-app and allows extra customer-service steps for highly regulated apps. Play wants an in-app path plus a working web link entered in the Data safety form, with retention practices disclosed.
findings.evidence: Apple says 'only offering to temporarily deactivate or disable an account is insufficient' and 'Apps in highly regulated industries... may use additional customer service flows'. Play requires developers to 'provide a web link resource where users can request app account deletion', and that link must reference the app or developer name.

findings.claim: Since 1 May 2024, App Store Connect rejects uploads that use required-reason APIs without declared reasons. The installed Expo SDK 57 and React Native 0.86 modules already ship privacy manifests for UserDefaults, file timestamp, system boot time and disk space.
findings.evidence: Apple: 'Starting May 1, 2024, apps that don't describe their use of required reason API in their privacy manifest file aren't accepted by App Store Connect.' A local scan of node_modules found PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in expo-constants (CA92.1), expo-device (35F9.1), expo-file-system (0A2A.1, 3B52.1, E174.1, 85F4.1), expo-system-ui (CA92.1) and react-native (C617.1, CA92.1, 35F9.1). Expo's docs say dependencies may still need their reasons added in app config.

findings.claim: On Play, READ_MEDIA_IMAGES and READ_MEDIA_VIDEO are only allowed when broad media access is the app's core function, enforced since 28 May 2025. The installed Expo modules do not declare those permissions; they declare CAMERA and legacy storage permissions capped at maxSdkVersion 32, except expo-image.
findings.evidence: The policy says apps 'may only request the READ_MEDIA_IMAGES and READ_MEDIA_VIDEO permissions if system pickers' are insufficient. A local manifest scan found that expo-image-picker declares CAMERA plus READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with maxSdk 32, and expo-image declares READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE with no maxSdk.

findings.claim: Both stores ban false or misleading functionality, and labelling something as being for entertainment does not get around the rule. A practice or demo build must say clearly everywhere that it uses simulated money.
findings.evidence: Apple 1.1.6: 'Stating that the app is "for entertainment purposes" won't overcome this guideline.' Apple 2.3.1(a) bans promoting services the app 'does not actually offer'. Play Deceptive Behavior: 'Any claim that an app is a "prank", "for entertainment purposes"... does not exempt'.

findings.claim: Contests are regulated on both stores. Apple requires sweepstakes and contests to be sponsored by the developer, with official rules that disclaim Apple. Play bans games that accept money for a chance at a prize and requires blocking minors from real-money contests. On Apple's age-rating questionnaire, frequent contests produce at least a 13+ rating.
findings.evidence: Apple 5.3.1 and 5.3.2 cover sponsorship and official rules. Apple's age-ratings page puts 'Infrequent simulated gambling; frequent contests' at 13+. Play's Real-Money Gambling, Games and Contests policy and its Age-Restricted Content policy cover the rest.

findings.claim: Platform minimums for 2026: Apple uploads must be built with Xcode 26 and the iOS 26 SDK (since 28 Apr 2026) and target iOS 13 or later (since 9 Sep 2026). New Play apps and updates must target API 36 from 31 Aug 2026, with extensions available to 1 Nov 2026. Apps distributed in the EU must have Apple trader status.
findings.evidence: These dates come from Apple's upcoming-requirements page and Play's target-API page. Apple's page also says 'Apps without trader status will be removed from the App Store in the European Union'.

findings.claim: (Inference) A university organization account fixes the account-type problem but not the licensing problem. Apple wants the app submitted by the entity that provides the financial service, and a university is not that entity. A public real-money release in any of the 8 markets therefore needs a licensed partner, such as a sponsor bank, broker or payment service provider, to provide the service and be the publisher or legal entity of record.
findings.evidence: This follows from 5.1.1(ix) and 3.2.1(viii) ('submitted by the financial institution performing such services') and from Play's rule to 'comply with state and local regulations' in every targeted country.

findings.claim: (Inference) A store-listed 'Practice' build with no real money, no bank link and no live merchant payments probably falls outside the 'provide services' wording of 5.1.1(ix). App Review may still apply it because the app looks like a fintech, so an organization account and very clear simulation labelling reduce the risk.
findings.evidence: The guideline text is about apps that 'provide services' in regulated fields. Whether a simulator is covered is not stated in Apple's documents; this is our judgement.

spec:
## How to read this

- **Fact**: a requirement quoted or paraphrased from the primary-source page in the Source column. Every page was fetched on 2026-10-10. The Apple Review Guidelines page says "Last updated June 8, 2026".
- **[I]**: our inference about what the requirement means for Vaultwise. These are not store text. Treat them as engineering judgement and check them with your advisor or a lawyer.
- The local evidence comes from this repo: `C:\Users\shaik\VaultWise\mobile\app.json`, `package.json`, and a scan of `node_modules/**/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` and the Android manifests.
- Research limit: the web-search budget for this session ran out, so every page here was fetched directly from developer.apple.com, support.google.com, developer.android.com, play.google and docs.expo.dev. Items I could not verify from a primary source are listed under Open questions.

---

## 1. Verdict

**Blockers for a student team (public, real-money release):**
1. **Apple 5.1.1(ix) and 3.2.1(viii)**: banking, financial services, investing and money-management apps "should be submitted by a legal entity that provides the services, and not by an individual developer" or by "the financial institution performing such services", with licences in every storefront. Real-money vaults, the Core ETF SIP, bank-debit round-ups and Pay with Vaultwise are all caught by this. [I] An individual account will be rejected. A university account still is not the entity providing the service.
2. **Apple 2.2**: "Demos, betas, and trial versions of your app don't belong on the App Store – use TestFlight instead."
3. **Play**: providers of financial products "should" use an organization account (D-U-N-S, up to 30 days). The app must "comply with state and local regulations for any region or country that your app targets", which here means 8 markets.
4. **iOS NFC tap-to-pay**: requires an organization, a payment licence or a binding agreement with a licensed payment service provider, and a commercial agreement with Apple. A student team cannot meet this in any of the 8 markets.

**Compliant fallback (recommended): "Vaultwise Practice"**
- **What the build does:** simulated balances, no bank linking or debits, receipt and invoice verification that releases simulated funds, a sandbox merchant checkout using test merchants and QR codes, and Satellite as paper trading clearly labelled as practice.
- **Labelling:** "Practice mode – no real money" must appear on every money screen and in the store text (Apple 1.1.6 and 2.3.1; Play Deceptive Behavior).
- **iOS distribution:** TestFlight internal testing, up to 100 App Store Connect users with no review needed for internal-only builds. Add external testing (up to 10,000 people) if you need it; the first external build is reviewed against the Guidelines. Builds expire after 90 days.
- **Android distribution:** Play internal testing (up to 100 testers; may skip standard review; exempt from Data safety). Move to Play closed testing if you need more testers; that requires Data safety and the Financial features declaration, and production access for new personal accounts needs 12 testers opted in for 14 days. You can also use an Android limited distribution account (free, up to 20 devices, no government ID) to sideload. This matters in Singapore after 2026-09-30.
- **If the class requires a public listing:** publish the Practice build only, under a university organization account (D-U-N-S; Apple fee waiver possible if the app is free). Describe it as a financial-literacy simulator. [I] Review risk remains.
- **Real money:** only possible later, with a licensed partner (sponsor bank or EMI, a broker for the SIP, a payment service provider) acting as the provider and publisher of record.

---

## 3. Build changes for the Practice build (concrete)

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Build flavor | `APP_VARIANT=practice` in EAS. Separate bundle ID (for example `app.vaultwise.practice`), app name "Vaultwise Practice", and a "PRACTICE" banner on every money screen. |
| Money movement | No Plaid or open-banking calls, no debits. Round-ups and auto-rules run against a simulated ledger. Merchant checkout runs only against sandbox merchants. |
| Satellite | Practice only. No prizes, no fees. Show the "Simulated prices – not investment advice" footer. |
| Core SIP | Simulated portfolio with real index prices. No order routing. |
| AI | Consent sheet naming Groq before first use (Apple 5.1.2(i)). In-chat "Report" button (Play AI policy). Prompt guardrails against personalized buy/sell advice. Redact PII before sending. |
| Age | DOB gate (18+) at signup. Declared Age Range (iOS) and Play Age Signals (Android) where they return signals. Apple override to 18+. Play target audience 18+ with Restrict Minor Access. |
| Deletion | Keep the in-app Settings → Delete account. Add a web deletion page and enter its URL in Play Data safety. |
| Privacy | Privacy policy URL in-app and in both consoles. Apple label and Play Data safety per rows 26–27. Check the privacy manifest after prebuild. |
| Payments UI | QR scan through `expo-camera` (already configured with barcode scanning). No NFC entitlement. |

## 4. Distribution plan (fallbacks ranked)

1. **Capstone demo (no store review):** TestFlight internal (up to 100 App Store Connect users) plus Play internal testing (up to 100), on an individual or university account.
2. **Wider beta:** TestFlight external (up to 10,000; first build reviewed) plus Play closed testing (Data safety and Financial features declaration required; if on a personal account, 12 testers for 14 days before production).
3. **Sideload:** Android limited distribution account (free, up to 20 devices, no ID). Required for Singapore testers outside Play after 2026-09-30.
4. **Public listing (optional):** Practice build only, under a university organization account (Apple: D-U-N-S, fee waiver possible; Play: organization account, D-U-N-S). Rated 18+, labelled as a simulator. [I] There is a residual 5.1.1(ix) review risk.
5. **Real money (post-capstone):** a licensed partner per market provides the services and is the submitting legal entity (Apple 5.1.1(ix) and 3.2.1(viii)), with full Play Financial features declaration and local licensing.
